# GitHub Copilot Instructions Template

This file provides workspace-level instructions for GitHub Copilot. Customize these instructions based on your project's needs.

## Code Style and Standards

- Follow the project's established coding conventions
- Write clear, self-documenting code with meaningful variable and function names
- Add comments only when necessary to explain complex logic or business rules
- Ensure code is modular and follows the single responsibility principle

## Documentation Standards

- Keep documentation up-to-date with code changes
- Use clear, concise language
- Include code examples where appropriate
- Document assumptions and edge cases

## Testing Guidelines

- Write tests for new features and bug fixes
- Follow the existing test structure and naming conventions
- Aim for meaningful test coverage
- Include both positive and negative test cases

## Security Practices

- Never commit secrets, API keys, or sensitive data
- Validate and sanitize all user inputs
- Follow security best practices for the project's language and framework
- Use parameterized queries to prevent SQL injection
- Implement proper authentication and authorization

## Git Commit Messages

- Use clear, descriptive commit messages
- Start with a verb in imperative mood (e.g., "Add", "Fix", "Update")
- Keep the first line under 50 characters
- Add detailed explanation in the body if needed

## Code Review Focus

- Check for potential bugs and edge cases
- Verify error handling is appropriate
- Ensure code is readable and maintainable
- Confirm tests are adequate
- Look for security vulnerabilities
